label: monk2-s7
resisted: Nothing unexplained. Veto gate 288 takes the a4/a5 pool node as input so sits in a serial composition rather than a leaf. Small veto leak: when the two active indicators are a2=1 and a5=1 the veto outputs 0.62 (x4.009 = 2.49 > ramp margin 1.56), giving 4/432 configurations (3 train rows) as false negatives.
tool_bugs: None. Limitation: a leaf cannot take another leaf's exit as an entry, so serial chains are compositions.
rule_agreement: 428/432 configurations agree with the MONK-2 rule; all 4 disagreements are a2=1 & a5=1 veto-leak cases. Implements the window in reverse to the paper's model: descending ramp sets the upper edge, low-count veto sets the lower edge.
summary: Output = sigmoid(1.383 + Ramp - 4.009 Veto - 0.888 Pool). Ramp is a descending linear count of first-value indicators (positive only when <=2 active); Pool is a rectified count of I4 and I5; Veto fires when <=1 indicator is active and overrides the ramp. Net: a window on exactly two active indicators. Train accuracy 0.991, AUC 1.0.
